blocks.source: 【RPG制作講座】作品を完成させる！
blocks.translation: 【RPG Design Guides】Complete Your Game!

blocks.source: 制作初心者にとっての最大の壁。それは『作品を完成させること』である。
blocks.translation: The biggest obstacle for beginners to game development is completing a game.

blocks.source: Web上で開発記録を公開しているような作品は多数あれど、その内、完成に漕ぎ着ける例はそれほど多くない。Webで公開なんてことをやっているからには、それなりにやる気もあるのだろうけれど、それでも完成にはなかなか至らない。
blocks.translation: There are many games whose development logs are published online, but relatively few ever reach completion. If someone is motivated enough to publish their development online, you would expect them to have a decent amount of drive, yet they still often fail to finish.

blocks.source: はっきり言って、この界隈では制作を中途放棄する人を見ることは珍しくも何ともない。それこそ制作の中途挫折を意味する『エターなる（エターナるが正？）』なんて言葉が定着してしまったほど。
blocks.translation: To be frank, it is hardly unusual in this community to see people abandon their projects midway. In fact, the term “eternal” (or is “eternaling” the correct form?), meaning to give up on a project partway through, has become firmly established.

blocks.source: ※エターなるの由来は特に説明しませんが、ググれば出てきます。
blocks.translation: ※I will not explain the origin of “eternal,” but you can find it by Googling it.

blocks.source: これを読んでいる方だって、制作経験があるならば、途中で投げ出した経験の一度や二度はあることだろう。この巨大な壁を乗り越えるため『作品を完成させること』を考察していきたい。
blocks.translation: If you have any development experience, you have probably given up on a project once or twice yourself. To overcome this enormous obstacle, I would like to examine what it means to complete a game.

blocks.source: ※この記事はエターなる経験者にとって、肺腑をえぐるような表現が含まれている可能性がなきにしもあらずです。ご注意ください。
blocks.translation: ※This article may contain expressions that cut particularly deeply for those who have experienced “eternaling.” Please be warned.

blocks.source: 目次
blocks.translation: Table of Contents

blocks.source: そもそも完成させるべきなのか？
blocks.translation: Should You Complete Your Game in the First Place?

blocks.source: 「別に完成しなくてもいいじゃないか。中途半端な作品なんて放り出してしまえ。それでも経験は積んでいるのだから、いずれ何年後かに自分の理想とする一作ができればいい」そんな考え方をする人もあるかもしれない。
blocks.translation: “It is not as though I have to finish it. I can just abandon an unfinished game. I will still gain experience, so eventually, years from now, I can make the one game I truly envision.” Some people may think this way.

blocks.source: だけど、それでもやはり作品は完成させるべきだと思う。
blocks.translation: Even so, I still think you should finish your game.

blocks.source: ゲーム制作には、最後まで完成させることで初めて勉強になる部分がある。たとえば「終盤のバランスの取り方」「エンディングによる物語の締め方」などだ。
blocks.translation: There are aspects of game development that you can only learn by completing a game all the way to the end—for example, how to balance the latter part of the game and how to bring the story to a close with the ending.

blocks.source: そして何より、完成作を人にプレイしてもらい、感想をもらうことによる恩恵が大きい。なんせ、初めて完成させた作品というものは、プレイヤーのことを顧みない自己中なものになりがち。
blocks.translation: Above all, having people play your completed game and give you their impressions is highly beneficial. After all, a first completed game tends to be self-centered and disregard the player.

blocks.source: 「自分は何十～何百時間と苦労したのだから、プレイヤーにも多少の面倒はかけてもいいだろう。このダンジョンでは２時間ぐらい迷ってもらおう」
blocks.translation: “I worked on this for dozens or even hundreds of hours, so it is fine to inconvenience the player a little. I think I will make them get lost in this dungeon for about two hours.”

blocks.source: これは凄くありがちな思考パターン。そのくせ自分のテストプレイでは、最短ルートを通って１０分で抜けてたりすると始末が悪い。プレイヤーにそっぽを向かれる経験を積んで、こういうのは矯正されていく。
blocks.translation: This is an extremely common way of thinking. It is even worse when the creator gets through the same dungeon in ten minutes by taking the shortest route during their own test play. Experiences of having players turn away from your game gradually correct this kind of thinking.

blocks.source: そんなわけで、製作経験は多くあっても、完成経験が乏しいようでは十分な経験があるとは言い難い。
blocks.translation: For that reason, even if you have a great deal of development experience, it is difficult to call it sufficient experience if you have little experience completing games.

blocks.source: 『作品を完成させる』というのも大事な技術の一つ。
blocks.translation: “Completing a game” is itself an important skill.

blocks.source: たとえ、何千時間と努力していても、作品を完成させる方法を知らなくては、同じことの繰り返しになりかねないというわけだ。
blocks.translation: In other words, even if you put in thousands of hours of effort, if you do not know how to complete a game, you may end up repeating the same cycle.

blocks.source: 世間には、作品を途中で放り出すことを繰り返しているプロの作家や漫画家もいるが、そうなるとクリエイターかつ社会人としての信用は大きく落ちてしまう。
blocks.translation: There are professional authors and manga artists who repeatedly abandon their works partway through, but when that happens, their credibility as both creators and members of society drops considerably.

blocks.source: 「どうせ、また投げ出すんだろ？」
blocks.translation: “You are going to give up again, right?”

blocks.source: 「こいつに仕事を依頼するのはやめておこう」
blocks.translation: “Let us not hire this person.”

blocks.source: ……となってしまう。
blocks.translation: …and that is what happens.

blocks.source: アマチュアのゲーム作家にしても、きちんとした完成作があるかないかで、信頼度は段違い。これは特に協力者を募りたい場合に重要となる。
blocks.translation: Even for amateur game creators, their credibility is vastly different depending on whether they have a properly completed game. This is especially important when they want to recruit collaborators.

blocks.source: やはり、妥協があってもよいから作品は完成させたい。
blocks.translation: Ultimately, I want to complete my games, even if that means making compromises.

blocks.source: で、この記事を書いている当人はどうかというと、エターなる率はかなり低いほうだと思う。ＲＰＧ以外も含めると、中学生の頃にエターなったのを最後に１０作品程度を連続で完成させている。
blocks.translation: So, what about me, the person writing this article? I believe my rate of abandoning projects is quite low. Including projects other than RPGs, I have completed around ten games in a row since the last time I abandoned one in middle school.

blocks.source: ＲＰＧツクールだろうが、ＳＲＰＧツクールだろうが、３Ｄシューティングツクールだろうが、デザエモンだろうが、開発に５０時間以上かけた作品は全て完成させたと記憶している。たとえ、つまらない作品だろうがとにかく完成させている。
blocks.translation: Whether it was RPG Maker, SRPG Maker, 3D Shooting Maker, or Dezaemon, I remember completing every project on which I spent more than 50 hours in development. Even if a game was boring, I completed it regardless.

blocks.source: そんな僕なりにエターならない作り方を考えてみた。あくまで完成経験に乏しい人を対象に書いているので、ある程度の完成経験があるという人はこの限りではない。
blocks.translation: With that in mind, I thought about how I avoid abandoning projects. I am writing this specifically for people with little experience completing games, so this may not apply to those with a moderate amount of completion experience.

blocks.source: いきなり大作にしない
blocks.translation: Do Not Start with a Huge Project

blocks.source: いきなり大作を目指さない。もし、長編を作るならば年単位の製作期間を覚悟しなければならないが、簡単にできることではない。
blocks.translation: Do not aim for a huge project right away. If you want to make a long game, you must be prepared to spend years developing it, but that is not something you can do easily.

blocks.source: 目指すのが短編だろうが長編だろうが、まずは小さな話を作ろう。舞台は世界より大陸。大陸より島。島より町。というように最初は小さな範囲で考えていこう。
blocks.translation: Whether you intend to make a short or long game, start by creating a small story. Make the setting a continent rather than the whole world, an island rather than a continent, or a town rather than an island. In other words, begin by thinking on a small scale.

blocks.source: 小さな話を完成させた後で、まだまだ長くしたいと思えたならば、そこから拡張していくような作り方をすればいい。長編だって、短編の集まりのようなものなのだから。
blocks.translation: After completing a small story, if you still want to make it longer, you can expand it from there. Even a long game is essentially a collection of short stories.

blocks.source: 例えば……
blocks.translation: For example…

blocks.source: 村娘が魔物にさらわれる。
blocks.translation: A village girl is kidnapped by monsters.

blocks.source: 魔物を退治して、村娘を助ける。
blocks.translation: Defeat the monsters and rescue the village girl.

blocks.source: 村娘と一緒に捕らわれていた謎の少女が実は王女だった。
blocks.translation: The mysterious girl who was being held captive with the village girl turns out to be a princess.

blocks.source: 王女を城に返しに行くことに。
blocks.translation: You decide to return the princess to the castle.

blocks.source: 城では国王が病に倒れ、不穏な空気が……。
blocks.translation: At the castle, the king has fallen ill, and an ominous atmosphere hangs in the air…

blocks.source: こんな感じでどんどんと繋げていく。やる気がなくなれば「２．」の段階で短編として完成させればよいというわけだ。
blocks.translation: You keep connecting events like this. If you lose motivation, you can simply complete it as a short game at step 2.

blocks.source: 骨格を作る
blocks.translation: Build the Framework

blocks.source: 優先して『ストーリー』『マップ』『必要なゲームシステム』といった骨格となる部分を作ろう。これらさえできれば、作品の形はできてくるので、後の部分は何とかなる。それ以外の重要でない要素は後回しにしてもよい。
blocks.translation: Prioritize creating the foundational elements: the story, maps, and necessary game systems. Once these are in place, the game will begin to take shape, and you can manage the remaining parts somehow. Less important elements can be postponed.

blocks.source: 逆に言えば、骨格ではない部分の制作に逃げてはならない。
blocks.translation: Conversely, you must not escape into creating parts that are not part of the framework.

blocks.source: 『逃げる』とは本編のストーリーもマップもロクにできていない段階から、寄り道要素を盛り込んでみたり、ひたすらアイテムや敵のデータばかり作ること。そうやって、いつまでも本編に着手しないような行為を指す。
blocks.translation: “Escaping” means adding side content when the main story and maps are barely developed, or endlessly creating item and enemy data. It refers to behavior that keeps you from ever starting work on the main game.

blocks.source: 自分の経験則だが、制作初心者には『隠し要素』や『寄り道要素』といったものをやたらと作りたがる人が多い気がする。どうも市販ＲＰＧにはお決まりのようにあるからなのか、真似したくなるらしい。
blocks.translation: This is based on my own experience, but I feel that many beginners are unusually eager to create “secret elements” and “side content.” Perhaps because commercial RPGs include them as a matter of course, they want to imitate them.

blocks.source: 当然ながら、こういった要素は作品の完成が見えてから盛り込めば十分。まともに完成していない作品に対して、寄り道要素やクリア後の隠し要素が充実していたって仕方がない。
blocks.translation: Naturally, there is no need to add these elements until the game is clearly nearing completion. There is little point in filling an unfinished game with side content or post-game secrets.

blocks.source: とにかく本編を作ろう。
blocks.translation: Above all, make the main game.

blocks.source: 省略できるように作る
blocks.translation: Design It So You Can Cut Content

blocks.source: 『いきなり大作にしない』に書いたのとは別の方法も紹介。やる気をなくした時は省略してでも完成させる。あるいは、省略できるように最初から作っておく。
blocks.translation: Here is another method besides the one described under “Do Not Start with a Huge Project.” When you lose motivation, complete the game even if you have to cut content. Alternatively, design it from the beginning so that content can be cut.

blocks.source: 例えば……
blocks.translation: For example…

blocks.source: 「魔王のしもべである十魔将と戦い、最後に魔王と決着をつける」という壮大なストーリーを考えていたとする。制作途中で飽きた場合は『十魔将』を『四魔将』に減らしてでも完成させてしまおう。
blocks.translation: Suppose you have devised an epic story in which you fight the Ten Generals of Evil, servants of the Demon King, and finally settle the score with the Demon King. If you get bored during development, complete the game even if you have to reduce the “Ten Generals of Evil” to the “Four Generals of Evil.”

blocks.source: 要するに、物語の最初と最後を先に考えておき、間は中抜きできるように作ってしまうという方法だ。
blocks.translation: In short, think of the beginning and end of the story first, and structure the middle so that it can be cut out.

blocks.source: 細部にこだわらない
blocks.translation: Don't Obsess Over Details

blocks.source: 過剰なリアリティなど、細部にこだわって自分の首を絞めない。
blocks.translation: Don't make things harder for yourself by obsessing over details such as excessive realism.

blocks.source: 例えば……
blocks.translation: For example...

blocks.source: この町は大都市だから、住民を１００人配置しよう。
blocks.translation: This is a major city, so let's place 100 residents here.

blocks.source: 民家は現実と同じように二階建てが当たり前。
blocks.translation: Houses should naturally have two floors, just like in real life.

blocks.source: もちろん、寝るところやトイレ・浴槽も必ずなくてはならない。
blocks.translation: Of course, every house must have a place to sleep, a toilet, and a bathtub.

blocks.source: 時刻の概念を導入しよう。
blocks.translation: Let's introduce the concept of time.

blocks.source: 町人は話しかける度にランダムで違う内容を話すようにしよう。
blocks.translation: Let's make townspeople say different things at random every time they're spoken to.

blocks.source: 食料と満腹度の概念を導入しよう。
blocks.translation: Let's introduce the concepts of food and fullness.

blocks.source: 全ての防具には斬打突炎氷……というように超詳細な耐性をつけよう。
blocks.translation: Let's give every piece of armor extremely detailed resistances, such as slash, strike, pierce, fire, ice...

blocks.source: ゲームシステムとして面白くできるという自信があるならともかく、単なるこだわりで細部まで作業を増やすのはお勧めできない。こういうのを目指すのは作品を完成できるようになってからでいい。
blocks.translation: Unless you're confident that you can make it interesting as a game system, I don't recommend increasing the workload down to the smallest details just because you feel particular about them. It's fine to aim for this kind of thing after you've learned how to complete a project.

blocks.source: 一度、作品を完成させれば「どれぐらいの手間がかかるか？」という現実も見えてくるはず。
blocks.translation: Once you've completed a project, you'll probably gain a realistic sense of how much effort it takes.

blocks.source: 複雑なイベントは避ける
blocks.translation: Avoid Complex Events

blocks.source: 複雑になりそうなイベントは無理して作らないようにしよう。実力を大きく越えて複雑なイベントを作ろうとすると、中途挫折の決め手になりやすい。
blocks.translation: Don't force yourself to create events that look like they will become complicated. Trying to create events that are far beyond your abilities is a common path to giving up halfway through.

blocks.source: よく使われるイベントで難易度が高いものの例を挙げてみる。
blocks.translation: Here are some examples of commonly used events that are difficult to create.

blocks.source: 武闘大会
blocks.translation: Martial Arts Tournament

blocks.source: いわゆる『天下一武道会』など、漫画でもゲームでもおなじみの展開。これをやろうという人も多いと思う。しかし、『大会会場のマップ』『控室などでの他出場者との会話』『大量の観客』『戦闘毎の会話』『複数回の戦闘』などなど、きっちり作ろうとすると、かなり大変なイベントである。
blocks.translation: The so-called "World Martial Arts Tournament" is a familiar scenario in both manga and games. I imagine many people want to include one. However, creating the tournament venue map, conversations with other contestants in the waiting room, a large audience, conversations during each battle, multiple battles, and so on makes this a very demanding event to build properly.

blocks.source: もっとも、このイベントは手を抜ける部分も多い。例えば、受付で会話後に画面転換して戦闘させるだけなら大して手間はかからない。武闘大会とは少し違うけど、ＦＦ６の『竜の首コロシアム』なんて、とってもシンプル。
blocks.translation: That said, there are many parts of this event where you can cut corners. For example, it wouldn't take much effort to have a conversation at the reception desk, transition to the battle screen, and start a battle. It's not quite a martial arts tournament, but Final Fantasy VI's Dragon's Neck Coliseum is very simple.

blocks.source: 戦争
blocks.translation: War

blocks.source: 物語において、国家同士あるいは人間対魔物のような騒乱を描く必要があることは多い。そこで必要となるのが戦争イベント。けれど、やっぱりこのイベントも大変。なんせ大量の兵隊を扱う必要があるのだ。配置するだけでも一苦労。さらに細かい動きをさせるなら、もっと苦労。
blocks.translation: Stories often need to depict conflicts between nations, or between humans and monsters. That's where a war event comes in. But this event is difficult too. After all, you need to handle a large number of soldiers. Just placing them is a challenge; making them perform detailed movements is even more difficult.

blocks.source: 主人公達も参加するイベントの場合は、ゲーム的にどう折り合いをつけるのかというのも難しい。比較的、楽なところでは……
blocks.translation: When the protagonists also participate in the event, it's difficult to work out how to handle it from a gameplay perspective. Some relatively easy options include...

blocks.source: 味方の軍を陽動にして、自分達は少数精鋭で敵地に潜入する。
blocks.translation: Use your army as a diversion while you infiltrate enemy territory with a small elite force.

blocks.source: 戦場を駆け巡って敵司令官を倒す。
blocks.translation: Race across the battlefield and defeat the enemy commander.

blocks.source: シンボルエンカウント＆ランダムエンカウントで敵が大勢いることを表現。
blocks.translation: Use symbol and random encounters to show that there are many enemies.

blocks.source: サガフロンティア２や幻想水滸伝のように、別システムでのシミュレーション型戦闘を用意しようなんて考えると大変だ。
blocks.translation: Trying to prepare simulation-style battles using a separate system, like in SaGa Frontier 2 or Suikoden, would be very difficult.

blocks.source: こういったイベントをやろうとして大変さに挫折したという人、いないだろうか？ かくいう僕も無理に武闘大会をやろうとして、挫折したことがあったりするのだけど……。
blocks.translation: Has anyone ever tried to create an event like this, only to give up because it was too much work? I myself once tried to force a martial arts tournament into a project and ended up giving up on it...

blocks.source: 難しそうなイベントは着手する前に、どんなシーンがあって、どんな作業が必要となるかよく考えておこう。手に負えないと思ったならば、他の簡単なイベントにするか、手を抜けるところを探してみよう。
blocks.translation: Before starting work on an event that seems difficult, think carefully about what scenes it will contain and what work will be required. If it seems beyond your abilities, either replace it with another, simpler event or look for parts where you can cut corners.

blocks.source: 効率の悪いシステムは避ける
blocks.translation: Avoid Inefficient Systems

blocks.source: 効率の悪いシステム設計を避けて、効率の良いシステムを目指す。
blocks.translation: Avoid inefficient system designs and aim for efficient ones.

blocks.source: 「効率の悪いシステムってなんぞ？」と思われたかもしれないが、具体的にはＤＱ６のように「制作の手間がかかる割にプレイヤーからの評価が上がらないシステム」のことを指す。
blocks.translation: You may be wondering, "What exactly is an inefficient system?" Specifically, I mean systems like the one in Dragon Quest VI: systems that take a lot of effort to create without earning much appreciation from players.

blocks.source: ＤＱ６には『多人数の仲間システム』と『転職システム』という二つのシステムが並立しているが、転職による職業の個性が、仲間の個性を潰してしまっていると言われることが多い。
blocks.translation: Dragon Quest VI has two systems running side by side: a system with many party members and a job-change system. However, it is often said that the individuality of the jobs obtained through job changes undermines the individuality of the party members.

blocks.source: 結果的に『仲間の個性に特化したＤＱ４』『職業の個性に特化したＤＱ３』などの作品と比較しても、システム評価が高いとは言えない。
blocks.translation: As a result, even compared with games such as Dragon Quest IV, which specializes in unique party members, and Dragon Quest III, which specializes in unique jobs, its system cannot be said to be highly regarded.

blocks.source: しかし、ＤＱ６のシステム制作にかかる手間はこの二作を大きく超えているだろうことは想像に難くない。
blocks.translation: However, it's not hard to imagine that the effort required to create Dragon Quest VI's systems far exceeded that required for those other two games.

blocks.source: システムを設計する際はこういった二つの要素が競合しないシンプルな設計にするとよいだろう。その方が少ない手間で作品を面白くしやすい。もちろん完成もしやすい。
blocks.translation: When designing a system, it's best to keep it simple so that these two elements don't compete with each other. That makes it easier to make the game interesting with less effort. Naturally, it also makes it easier to complete.

blocks.source: 無理に自作しない
blocks.translation: Don't Force Yourself to Create Everything

blocks.source: 経験が乏しい状態で、素材やゲームシステムをほぼ自作するというのはかなり厳しい。最初は無理せず、フリーの素材＆スクリプトを使用したり、開発ツールのデフォルト素材＆システムを中心とするほうが無難だろう。
blocks.translation: Creating most of your assets and game systems yourself with little experience is extremely difficult. At first, it's safer to use free assets and scripts, or to rely primarily on the default assets and systems included with your development tool.

blocks.source: もしやる場合でも、狭い範囲から挑戦していくとよいかと。
blocks.translation: Even if you do decide to create things yourself, I recommend starting with a limited scope.

blocks.source: 仲間メンバーのキャラグラだけ自作する。
blocks.translation: Create only the character graphics for your party members yourself.

blocks.source: 聞く頻度の多いフィールド曲だけ自作してみる。
blocks.translation: Try creating only the field music that players will hear frequently.

blocks.source: 戦闘はツールのデフォルトだが、成長システムは自作してみる。
blocks.translation: Use the tool's default battle system, but try creating your own progression system.

blocks.source: などなどだ。
blocks.translation: And so on.

blocks.source: グラフィックや音楽の差し替えは開発途中でも案外できる。開発終盤に余裕ができたのでやってみようという感じでもよいだろう。
blocks.translation: Replacing graphics and music is surprisingly feasible even during development. You could also wait until the end of development, when you have more time, and try it then.

blocks.source: モチベーション
blocks.translation: Motivation

blocks.source: 制作に対するモチベーションの持ち方についても書いておく。
blocks.translation: I'd also like to write about how to maintain motivation during development.

blocks.source: 「モチベーションを高くするにはどうしたらいいか？」というのは多くの人が思うところだろう。けれど、個人的な意見を言えば、そもそも無理に高いモチベーションを保つ必要はないと思っている。
blocks.translation: Many people probably wonder, "How can I stay highly motivated?" But personally, I don't think there's any need to force yourself to maintain a high level of motivation in the first place.

blocks.source: というのも、強いやる気を出して、一気に制作に取り掛かったところで、制作期間が一ヶ月～二ヶ月～三ヶ月と伸びていくに連れて、維持が難しくなってくる。『熱しやすく冷めやすい』なんて言葉の通り、冷めた時に挫折スイッチが入るのが関の山。
blocks.translation: The reason is that even if you become highly motivated and throw yourself into development all at once, it becomes increasingly difficult to maintain that motivation as development stretches from one month to two, then three. As the saying goes, "easy to heat and easy to cool"—once your enthusiasm fades, you're likely to hit the switch that makes you give up.

blocks.source: 特にいちいち何かやる度に、成果や反響を求めてしまう性格の人は要注意。
blocks.translation: People who feel the need to see results or receive feedback every time they do something in particular should be especially careful.

blocks.source: 反響があろうがなかろうが、黙々と地味な作業の連続に耐えられる根気がなければ、長編の完成は難しい。
blocks.translation: Whether or not you receive any feedback, it is difficult to complete a long game without the perseverance to endure a continuous stream of quiet, tedious work.

blocks.source: 何でこんなことを書くのかというと、
blocks.translation: The reason I'm writing this is that

blocks.source: 制作開始。
blocks.translation: Development begins.

blocks.source: 凄くはりきる。
blocks.translation: Get extremely fired up.

blocks.source: 徐々に制作のキツさが分かってくる。
blocks.translation: Gradually realize how grueling game development is.

blocks.source: だんだんクールダウン。
blocks.translation: Gradually cool down.

blocks.source: エターなる。
blocks.translation: Eternalize it.

blocks.source: というような制作初心者の必殺コンボを何度も見てきたからである。
blocks.translation: Because I have seen this sort of deadly combo used by beginner developers many times.

blocks.source: そんなわけで、普通のモチベーションで日課のように淡々と制作すれば十分かなと思っている。
blocks.translation: That being the case, I think it is enough to work steadily on development as part of my daily routine with an ordinary level of motivation.

blocks.source: もっとも、モチベーションの持ち方なんて、個人差があって当たり前なので、あくまで僕の意見ということで。もちろん、短期で制作できるような規模の作品ならば、一気にやるのもよし。
blocks.translation: That said, it is only natural for people to differ in how they maintain their motivation, so this is merely my opinion. Of course, if the project is small enough to complete in a short period, it is perfectly fine to work on it intensively.

blocks.source: もし、エターなったら？
blocks.translation: What if you abandon a project?

blocks.source: それでも、エターなってしまった場合も、データを削除するのだけはやめよう。もしかしたら、またいつか作品の制作を再開したくなることもあるかもしれない。その作品は永久凍結するにしても、部分的に流用できることもあるかもしれない。
blocks.translation: Even if you do abandon a project, whatever you do, do not delete the data. You may want to resume development someday. Even if the project is permanently shelved, parts of it may still be reusable.

blocks.source: そして重要なのは、自分が「なぜエターなってしまったのか？」という分析だ。
blocks.translation: What is important, though, is analyzing why you abandoned it.

blocks.source: ストーリーをうまく作れなかったため？
blocks.translation: Because you could not create the story well?

blocks.source: 書いた脚本が恥ずかしくなったため？
blocks.translation: Because you became embarrassed by the script you wrote?

blocks.source: マップ制作が面倒になったため？
blocks.translation: Because creating the maps became too much of a hassle?

blocks.source: やりたいシステムを実現する技術がなかったため？
blocks.translation: Because you lacked the technical skills to implement the systems you wanted?

blocks.source: 満足のいく素材が用意できなかったため？
blocks.translation: Because you could not prepare satisfactory assets?

blocks.source: クオリティに自信が持てなかったため？
blocks.translation: Because you lacked confidence in the quality?

blocks.source: 時間が取れなかったため？
blocks.translation: Because you could not make time for it?

blocks.source: エターなる理由も人それぞれだろうから、その対策も簡単には言えない。
blocks.translation: Since everyone has their own reasons for abandoning a project, it is not easy to say what countermeasures to take.

blocks.source: それでも、自己の分析こそが『脱エターナラー』の一歩となる。
blocks.translation: Even so, self-analysis is the first step toward becoming an ex-eternalizer.

blocks.source: 例えば、僕は「中学生の頃にエターなった」と書いたが、その理由は「ストーリーをうまく作れなかったため」というのが大きい。どうも、当時の僕はストーリーの制作にそこまで興味がなかったのだと思う。なので、ストーリーで無理をしない作品にすることで、次は完成させることができた。
blocks.translation: For example, I wrote that I “abandoned a project when I was in middle school,” and the main reason was that “I could not create the story well.” Apparently, I was not all that interested in creating stories back then. So, by making a project that did not push me too hard in terms of story, I was able to complete it the next time.

texts.制作初心者にとっての最大の壁。それは『作品を完成させること』である。: The biggest obstacle for beginners to game development is completing a game.
texts.Web上で開発記録を公開しているような作品は多数あれど、その内、完成に漕ぎ着ける: There are many games whose development logs are published online, but relatively few ever reach completion. If someone is motivated enough to publish their development online, you would expect them to have a decent amount of drive, yet they still often fail to finish.
texts.はっきり言って、この界隈では制作を中途放棄する人を見ることは珍しくも何ともない。: To be frank, it is hardly unusual in this community to see people abandon their projects midway. In fact, the term “eternal” (or is “eternaling” the correct form?), meaning to give up on a project partway through, has become firmly established.
texts.※エターなるの由来は特に説明しませんが、ググれば出てきます。: ※I will not explain the origin of “eternal,” but you can find it by Googling it.
texts.これを読んでいる方だって、制作経験があるならば、途中で投げ出した経験の一度や二度: If you have any development experience, you have probably given up on a project once or twice yourself. To overcome this enormous obstacle, I would like to examine what it means to complete a game.
texts.※この記事はエターなる経験者にとって、肺腑をえぐるような表現が含まれている可能性: ※This article may contain expressions that cut particularly deeply for those who have experienced “eternaling.” Please be warned.
texts.そもそも完成させるべきなのか？: Should You Complete Your Game in the First Place?
texts.「別に完成しなくてもいいじゃないか。中途半端な作品なんて放り出してしまえ。それで: “It is not as though I have to finish it. I can just abandon an unfinished game. I will still gain experience, so eventually, years from now, I can make the one game I truly envision.” Some people may think this way.
texts.だけど、それでもやはり作品は完成させるべきだと思う。: Even so, I still think you should finish your game.
texts.ゲーム制作には、最後まで完成させることで初めて勉強になる部分がある。たとえば「終: There are aspects of game development that you can only learn by completing a game all the way to the end—for example, how to balance the latter part of the game and how to bring the story to a close with the ending.
texts.そして何より、完成作を人にプレイしてもらい、感想をもらうことによる恩恵が大きい。: Above all, having people play your completed game and give you their impressions is highly beneficial. After all, a first completed game tends to be self-centered and disregard the player.
texts.「自分は何十～何百時間と苦労したのだから、プレイヤーにも多少の面倒はかけてもいい: “I worked on this for dozens or even hundreds of hours, so it is fine to inconvenience the player a little. I think I will make them get lost in this dungeon for about two hours.”
texts.これは凄くありがちな思考パターン。そのくせ自分のテストプレイでは、最短ルートを通: This is an extremely common way of thinking. It is even worse when the creator gets through the same dungeon in ten minutes by taking the shortest route during their own test play. Experiences of having players turn away from your game gradually correct this kind of thinking.
texts.そんなわけで、製作経験は多くあっても、完成経験が乏しいようでは十分な経験があると: For that reason, even if you have a great deal of development experience, it is difficult to call it sufficient experience if you have little experience completing games.
texts.『作品を完成させる』というのも大事な技術の一つ。: “Completing a game” is itself an important skill.
texts.たとえ、何千時間と努力していても、作品を完成させる方法を知らなくては、同じことの: In other words, even if you put in thousands of hours of effort, if you do not know how to complete a game, you may end up repeating the same cycle.
texts.世間には、作品を途中で放り出すことを繰り返しているプロの作家や漫画家もいるが、そ: There are professional authors and manga artists who repeatedly abandon their works partway through, but when that happens, their credibility as both creators and members of society drops considerably.
texts.「どうせ、また投げ出すんだろ？」: “You are going to give up again, right?”
texts.アマチュアのゲーム作家にしても、きちんとした完成作があるかないかで、信頼度は段違: Even for amateur game creators, their credibility is vastly different depending on whether they have a properly completed game. This is especially important when they want to recruit collaborators.
texts.やはり、妥協があってもよいから作品は完成させたい。: Ultimately, I want to complete my games, even if that means making compromises.
texts.で、この記事を書いている当人はどうかというと、エターなる率はかなり低いほうだと思: So, what about me, the person writing this article? I believe my rate of abandoning projects is quite low. Including projects other than RPGs, I have completed around ten games in a row since the last time I abandoned one in middle school.
texts.ＲＰＧツクールだろうが、ＳＲＰＧツクールだろうが、３Ｄシューティングツクールだろ: Whether it was RPG Maker, SRPG Maker, 3D Shooting Maker, or Dezaemon, I remember completing every project on which I spent more than 50 hours in development. Even if a game was boring, I completed it regardless.
texts.そんな僕なりにエターならない作り方を考えてみた。あくまで完成経験に乏しい人を対象: With that in mind, I thought about how I avoid abandoning projects. I am writing this specifically for people with little experience completing games, so this may not apply to those with a moderate amount of completion experience.
texts.いきなり大作にしない: Do Not Start with a Huge Project
texts.いきなり大作を目指さない。もし、長編を作るならば年単位の製作期間を覚悟しなければ: Do not aim for a huge project right away. If you want to make a long game, you must be prepared to spend years developing it, but that is not something you can do easily.
texts.目指すのが短編だろうが長編だろうが、まずは小さな話を作ろう。舞台は世界より大陸。: Whether you intend to make a short or long game, start by creating a small story. Make the setting a continent rather than the whole world, an island rather than a continent, or a town rather than an island. In other words, begin by thinking on a small scale.
texts.小さな話を完成させた後で、まだまだ長くしたいと思えたならば、そこから拡張していく: After completing a small story, if you still want to make it longer, you can expand it from there. Even a long game is essentially a collection of short stories.
texts.村娘が魔物にさらわれる。: A village girl is kidnapped by monsters.
texts.魔物を退治して、村娘を助ける。: Defeat the monsters and rescue the village girl.
texts.村娘と一緒に捕らわれていた謎の少女が実は王女だった。: The mysterious girl who was being held captive with the village girl turns out to be a princess.
texts.王女を城に返しに行くことに。: You decide to return the princess to the castle.
texts.城では国王が病に倒れ、不穏な空気が……。: At the castle, the king has fallen ill, and an ominous atmosphere hangs in the air…
texts.こんな感じでどんどんと繋げていく。やる気がなくなれば「２．」の段階で短編として完: You keep connecting events like this. If you lose motivation, you can simply complete it as a short game at step 2.
texts.優先して『ストーリー』『マップ』『必要なゲームシステム』といった骨格となる部分を: Prioritize creating the foundational elements: the story, maps, and necessary game systems. Once these are in place, the game will begin to take shape, and you can manage the remaining parts somehow. Less important elements can be postponed.
texts.逆に言えば、骨格ではない部分の制作に逃げてはならない。: Conversely, you must not escape into creating parts that are not part of the framework.
texts.『逃げる』とは本編のストーリーもマップもロクにできていない段階から、寄り道要素を: “Escaping” means adding side content when the main story and maps are barely developed, or endlessly creating item and enemy data. It refers to behavior that keeps you from ever starting work on the main game.
texts.自分の経験則だが、制作初心者には『隠し要素』や『寄り道要素』といったものをやたら: This is based on my own experience, but I feel that many beginners are unusually eager to create “secret elements” and “side content.” Perhaps because commercial RPGs include them as a matter of course, they want to imitate them.
texts.当然ながら、こういった要素は作品の完成が見えてから盛り込めば十分。まともに完成し: Naturally, there is no need to add these elements until the game is clearly nearing completion. There is little point in filling an unfinished game with side content or post-game secrets.
texts.とにかく本編を作ろう。: Above all, make the main game.
texts.省略できるように作る: Design It So You Can Cut Content
texts.『いきなり大作にしない』に書いたのとは別の方法も紹介。やる気をなくした時は省略し: Here is another method besides the one described under “Do Not Start with a Huge Project.” When you lose motivation, complete the game even if you have to cut content. Alternatively, design it from the beginning so that content can be cut.
texts.「魔王のしもべである十魔将と戦い、最後に魔王と決着をつける」という壮大なストーリ: Suppose you have devised an epic story in which you fight the Ten Generals of Evil, servants of the Demon King, and finally settle the score with the Demon King. If you get bored during development, complete the game even if you have to reduce the “Ten Generals of Evil” to the “Four Generals of Evil.”
texts.要するに、物語の最初と最後を先に考えておき、間は中抜きできるように作ってしまうと: In short, think of the beginning and end of the story first, and structure the middle so that it can be cut out.
texts.過剰なリアリティなど、細部にこだわって自分の首を絞めない。: Don't make things harder for yourself by obsessing over details such as excessive realism.
texts.この町は大都市だから、住民を１００人配置しよう。: This is a major city, so let's place 100 residents here.
texts.民家は現実と同じように二階建てが当たり前。: Houses should naturally have two floors, just like in real life.
texts.もちろん、寝るところやトイレ・浴槽も必ずなくてはならない。: Of course, every house must have a place to sleep, a toilet, and a bathtub.
texts.時刻の概念を導入しよう。: Let's introduce the concept of time.
texts.町人は話しかける度にランダムで違う内容を話すようにしよう。: Let's make townspeople say different things at random every time they're spoken to.
texts.食料と満腹度の概念を導入しよう。: Let's introduce the concepts of food and fullness.
texts.全ての防具には斬打突炎氷……というように超詳細な耐性をつけよう。: Let's give every piece of armor extremely detailed resistances, such as slash, strike, pierce, fire, ice...
texts.ゲームシステムとして面白くできるという自信があるならともかく、単なるこだわりで細: Unless you're confident that you can make it interesting as a game system, I don't recommend increasing the workload down to the smallest details just because you feel particular about them. It's fine to aim for this kind of thing after you've learned how to complete a project.
texts.一度、作品を完成させれば「どれぐらいの手間がかかるか？」という現実も見えてくるは: Once you've completed a project, you'll probably gain a realistic sense of how much effort it takes.
texts.複雑になりそうなイベントは無理して作らないようにしよう。実力を大きく越えて複雑な: Don't force yourself to create events that look like they will become complicated. Trying to create events that are far beyond your abilities is a common path to giving up halfway through.
texts.よく使われるイベントで難易度が高いものの例を挙げてみる。: Here are some examples of commonly used events that are difficult to create.
texts.いわゆる『天下一武道会』など、漫画でもゲームでもおなじみの展開。これをやろうとい: The so-called "World Martial Arts Tournament" is a familiar scenario in both manga and games. I imagine many people want to include one. However, creating the tournament venue map, conversations with other contestants in the waiting room, a large audience, conversations during each battle, multiple battles, and so on makes this a very demanding event to build properly.
texts.もっとも、このイベントは手を抜ける部分も多い。例えば、受付で会話後に画面転換して: That said, there are many parts of this event where you can cut corners. For example, it wouldn't take much effort to have a conversation at the reception desk, transition to the battle screen, and start a battle. It's not quite a martial arts tournament, but Final Fantasy VI's Dragon's Neck Coliseum is very simple.
texts.物語において、国家同士あるいは人間対魔物のような騒乱を描く必要があることは多い。: Stories often need to depict conflicts between nations, or between humans and monsters. That's where a war event comes in. But this event is difficult too. After all, you need to handle a large number of soldiers. Just placing them is a challenge; making them perform detailed movements is even more difficult.
texts.主人公達も参加するイベントの場合は、ゲーム的にどう折り合いをつけるのかというのも: When the protagonists also participate in the event, it's difficult to work out how to handle it from a gameplay perspective. Some relatively easy options include...
texts.味方の軍を陽動にして、自分達は少数精鋭で敵地に潜入する。: Use your army as a diversion while you infiltrate enemy territory with a small elite force.
texts.戦場を駆け巡って敵司令官を倒す。: Race across the battlefield and defeat the enemy commander.
texts.シンボルエンカウント＆ランダムエンカウントで敵が大勢いることを表現。: Use symbol and random encounters to show that there are many enemies.
texts.サガフロンティア２や幻想水滸伝のように、別システムでのシミュレーション型戦闘を用: Trying to prepare simulation-style battles using a separate system, like in SaGa Frontier 2 or Suikoden, would be very difficult.
texts.こういったイベントをやろうとして大変さに挫折したという人、いないだろうか？ かく: Has anyone ever tried to create an event like this, only to give up because it was too much work? I myself once tried to force a martial arts tournament into a project and ended up giving up on it...
texts.難しそうなイベントは着手する前に、どんなシーンがあって、どんな作業が必要となるか: Before starting work on an event that seems difficult, think carefully about what scenes it will contain and what work will be required. If it seems beyond your abilities, either replace it with another, simpler event or look for parts where you can cut corners.
texts.効率の悪いシステム設計を避けて、効率の良いシステムを目指す。: Avoid inefficient system designs and aim for efficient ones.
texts.「効率の悪いシステムってなんぞ？」と思われたかもしれないが、具体的にはＤＱ６のよ: You may be wondering, "What exactly is an inefficient system?" Specifically, I mean systems like the one in Dragon Quest VI: systems that take a lot of effort to create without earning much appreciation from players.
texts.ＤＱ６には『多人数の仲間システム』と『転職システム』という二つのシステムが並立し: Dragon Quest VI has two systems running side by side: a system with many party members and a job-change system. However, it is often said that the individuality of the jobs obtained through job changes undermines the individuality of the party members.
texts.結果的に『仲間の個性に特化したＤＱ４』『職業の個性に特化したＤＱ３』などの作品と: As a result, even compared with games such as Dragon Quest IV, which specializes in unique party members, and Dragon Quest III, which specializes in unique jobs, its system cannot be said to be highly regarded.
texts.しかし、ＤＱ６のシステム制作にかかる手間はこの二作を大きく超えているだろうことは: However, it's not hard to imagine that the effort required to create Dragon Quest VI's systems far exceeded that required for those other two games.
texts.システムを設計する際はこういった二つの要素が競合しないシンプルな設計にするとよい: When designing a system, it's best to keep it simple so that these two elements don't compete with each other. That makes it easier to make the game interesting with less effort. Naturally, it also makes it easier to complete.
texts.無理に自作しない: Don't Force Yourself to Create Everything
texts.経験が乏しい状態で、素材やゲームシステムをほぼ自作するというのはかなり厳しい。最: Creating most of your assets and game systems yourself with little experience is extremely difficult. At first, it's safer to use free assets and scripts, or to rely primarily on the default assets and systems included with your development tool.
texts.もしやる場合でも、狭い範囲から挑戦していくとよいかと。: Even if you do decide to create things yourself, I recommend starting with a limited scope.
texts.仲間メンバーのキャラグラだけ自作する。: Create only the character graphics for your party members yourself.
texts.聞く頻度の多いフィールド曲だけ自作してみる。: Try creating only the field music that players will hear frequently.
texts.戦闘はツールのデフォルトだが、成長システムは自作してみる。: Use the tool's default battle system, but try creating your own progression system.
texts.グラフィックや音楽の差し替えは開発途中でも案外できる。開発終盤に余裕ができたので: Replacing graphics and music is surprisingly feasible even during development. You could also wait until the end of development, when you have more time, and try it then.
texts.制作に対するモチベーションの持ち方についても書いておく。: I'd also like to write about how to maintain motivation during development.
texts.「モチベーションを高くするにはどうしたらいいか？」というのは多くの人が思うところ: Many people probably wonder, "How can I stay highly motivated?" But personally, I don't think there's any need to force yourself to maintain a high level of motivation in the first place.
texts.というのも、強いやる気を出して、一気に制作に取り掛かったところで、制作期間が一ヶ: The reason is that even if you become highly motivated and throw yourself into development all at once, it becomes increasingly difficult to maintain that motivation as development stretches from one month to two, then three. As the saying goes, "easy to heat and easy to cool"—once your enthusiasm fades, you're likely to hit the switch that makes you give up.
texts.特にいちいち何かやる度に、成果や反響を求めてしまう性格の人は要注意。: People who feel the need to see results or receive feedback every time they do something in particular should be especially careful.
texts.反響があろうがなかろうが、黙々と地味な作業の連続に耐えられる根気がなければ、長編: Whether or not you receive any feedback, it is difficult to complete a long game without the perseverance to endure a continuous stream of quiet, tedious work.
texts.何でこんなことを書くのかというと、: The reason I'm writing this is that
texts.徐々に制作のキツさが分かってくる。: Gradually realize how grueling game development is.
texts.というような制作初心者の必殺コンボを何度も見てきたからである。: Because I have seen this sort of deadly combo used by beginner developers many times.
texts.そんなわけで、普通のモチベーションで日課のように淡々と制作すれば十分かなと思って: That being the case, I think it is enough to work steadily on development as part of my daily routine with an ordinary level of motivation.
texts.もっとも、モチベーションの持ち方なんて、個人差があって当たり前なので、あくまで僕: That said, it is only natural for people to differ in how they maintain their motivation, so this is merely my opinion. Of course, if the project is small enough to complete in a short period, it is perfectly fine to work on it intensively.
texts.もし、エターなったら？: What if you abandon a project?
texts.それでも、エターなってしまった場合も、データを削除するのだけはやめよう。もしかし: Even if you do abandon a project, whatever you do, do not delete the data. You may want to resume development someday. Even if the project is permanently shelved, parts of it may still be reusable.
texts.そして重要なのは、自分が「なぜエターなってしまったのか？」という分析だ。: What is important, though, is analyzing why you abandoned it.
texts.ストーリーをうまく作れなかったため？: Because you could not create the story well?
texts.書いた脚本が恥ずかしくなったため？: Because you became embarrassed by the script you wrote?
texts.マップ制作が面倒になったため？: Because creating the maps became too much of a hassle?
texts.やりたいシステムを実現する技術がなかったため？: Because you lacked the technical skills to implement the systems you wanted?
texts.満足のいく素材が用意できなかったため？: Because you could not prepare satisfactory assets?
texts.クオリティに自信が持てなかったため？: Because you lacked confidence in the quality?
texts.時間が取れなかったため？: Because you could not make time for it?
texts.エターなる理由も人それぞれだろうから、その対策も簡単には言えない。: Since everyone has their own reasons for abandoning a project, it is not easy to say what countermeasures to take.
texts.それでも、自己の分析こそが『脱エターナラー』の一歩となる。: Even so, self-analysis is the first step toward becoming an ex-eternalizer.
texts.例えば、僕は「中学生の頃にエターなった」と書いたが、その理由は「ストーリーをうま: For example, I wrote that I “abandoned a project when I was in middle school,” and the main reason was that “I could not create the story well.” Apparently, I was not all that interested in creating stories back then. So, by making a project that did not push me too hard in terms of story, I was able to complete it the next time.
